refs.text: Bitcoin has now seen a 16 % decline from the overall high from $88 ,000, touching down towards about $73 ,400, $500, give or take.
refs.label: the protected preview (L-d, PBX 2026-11-11)

refs.text: Bitcoin does not have any authority that allows people to take the wealth of others. If some people end up with more Bitcoin, that's because they chose to do that.
refs.label: the protected moments reference 37c5b5f5

refs.text: Bitcoin imposes a global free market for the first time ever.
refs.label: the protected medley reference 41f29b1f

refs.text: A CEO makes a personal mistake in shareholders pay. A government mismanages its currencies. and its savers pay. Bitcoin's rules aren't kept by a single executive or a single central bank. They're enforced by thousands of independent computers running the same code. No CEO, no compromise, no committee to debate.
refs.label: the published medley 0c68b589

refs.text: Currencies are often born for political reasons, but fail for economic reasons. Bitcoin launched in January of 2009. It's never been renamed. It's never gone into another currency. It's never been redenominated or reissued.
